# Permanent OpenPGP decryption keeps a signed payload body instead of rebuilding its MIME children

The 41d2dd0 change saves the original decrypted Content-Type before inner protected-subject parsing can change ct. A multipart/signed payload keeps its returned body string and has subParts cleared, avoiding a new multipart/mixed wrapper and reserialization of signed child headers. Non-signed payloads keep the old wrapper path, and both update cryptoChanged. The persistent caller then serializes and copies the modified tree. This preserves the signed-body path, not every outer header or all serialization encodings. The added browser assertion checks a verified signature-icon source state; it does not directly assert forwarding, Edit as New or byte equality, and no fresh cryptographic test ran.

Scope: OpenPGP permanent decryption.
